I've farmed these 5 mu for 20 years, since I married into this village. I'm 44 now. I only finished primary school, but I know my land. My husband works in a factory in town and comes back for harvest and sowing. We have two children. We grow wheat in winter and maize in summer on all 5 mu — that's what everyone around here does.

For wheat, I sow in early October. I buy improved seed from the dealer in town, about 30 jin per mu. Before sowing, I hire my cousin's tractor to rotary till the field — costs 50 yuan per mu. I spread one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as basal. The dealer says it's 15-15-15 or something close to that. Then in March, when the wheat turns green, I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu. The dealer told me that's about 14 kg of nitrogen per mu altogether. For phosphorus and potassium, I just get what comes in the compound. I irrigate three times: once after sowing if it's dry, once in March at green-up, and once at heading in April or May. Pumping water costs money, so three times is what I always do. I spray herbicide once after sowing, insecticide twice in spring, and fungicide once if it looks rainy. Last year I got about 950 jin per mu. This year I hope for 1000 jin, about 480 kg per mu.

For maize, right after we cut the wheat in early June, there's no time to plow. I hire the machine to sow hybrid seed directly into the wheat stubble, no-tillage. I buy the seed in bags, about 1 bag per mu. I put compound fertilizer down at the same time, about one bag per mu. The maize compound has more nitrogen, like 27-6-7 or whatever the dealer has this year. That's about 12 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus some phosphorus and potassium. I don't usually add extra urea for maize. I irrigate twice — once when it's small if it's dry, and once at the big growth stage in July. I spray insecticide twice because corn borers are always a problem, and herbicide once. Last year my maize gave me about 1050 jin per mu, about 520 kg. I expect the same this year.

I think about costs all the time. A bag of compound is 130 yuan now, urea is cheaper but still money. If I spend too much on fertilizer, I don't have cash left for pesticide or for my daughter's school fees. But I also don't dare cut back too much — a bad harvest is worse than wasting some fertilizer. I watch what my neighbors do. Old Zhang down the road has good wheat every year, and he uses about the same as me, so I copy him. When I'm not sure, I do what I did last year. Change is risky.
